deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 10% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.9% = 10-year Treasury 4.9% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 46% last year; 57%/yr over 3 years — the market expects a slowdown from its recent pace.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 59% (3 years ago -6%, rising) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $59 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 107% (3 years ago -16%).

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags
flags: Profit leans on non-operating gains: net income $10.0B vs operating income $5.7B over the last 12 months (e.g. investment gains or one-offs that may not repeat).

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 57%/yr over 3 years and -4%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 39% vs a 5-year range of -68–39% (median 12%): near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back).

tiles.title: Sales growth
tiles.sub: latest quarter +67% vs a year earlier · 12-month sales $14.5B
tiles.read: Latest quarter: sales up 67% vs a year earlier and speeding up (from 45% two quarters ago): demand is strengthening.
tiles.explain: Headline: sales over the last 12 months vs the 12 months before. Bars: each quarter's sales vs the same quarter a year earlier.

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Each $100 of sales leaves $39 of operating profit, up from $28 a year ago: profitability is improving.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: Just 43% of reported profit became spare cash: much of the profit is tied up in spending or working capital.
tiles.explain: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus spending on equipment and buildings: money the company could return or reinvest.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: You pay 11× last year's profit (lower than 53% of the last 5 years); only 7× next year's forecast, so the market expects profits to jump.
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.

tiles.explain: Consensus = the average analyst forecast (Yahoo, unofficial). The typical move is the average size of the stock's next-day move after its last reports, not an options-implied figure.
